description: PII Data Exposure in Analytics and Logging PII data from customer interactions flows through various processing and analytics components without proper sanitization or encryption. This includes call recordings, chat transcripts, and customer profile data. An attacker with access to analytics dashboards or log files could extract sensitive customer information. Additionally, internal users with access to these systems could misuse or exfiltrate PII data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
mitreATT&CK: T1213 - Data from Information Repositories
recommendation: Implement PII data handling controls across the platform
recommendation: Enhance access controls and monitoring for PII data

description: Denial of Service Vulnerability Multiple public endpoints lack proper request rate limiting and could be overwhelmed by excessive traffic. The CDK code shows no usage of WAF or other DoS prevention mechanisms. An attacker could launch a DDoS attack against the API Gateway endpoints or Connect instance, disrupting service for legitimate users. Resource exhaustion could occur through repeated Lambda invocations or database connections.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service

description: Insufficient Resource Access Controls The CDK code shows broad IAM permissions and lacks fine-grained access controls for Connect integration with other AWS services. Service-linked roles are not consistently used. An attacker who compromises a Connect instance or gains access to an administrative account could potentially access or modify unauthorized AWS resources due to overly permissive IAM policies.
references: recommendation: Implement least privilege access control
recommendation: Enhanced access monitoring and control

description: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Chat Interface Malicious users could inject JavaScript code through chat messages that gets executed in the context of other users' browsers when rendered in the chat interface. An attacker sends a chat message containing malicious JavaScript that steals session cookies or performs actions on behalf of other users when the message is displayed in their chat window.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1059.007 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
recommendation: Enhanced security headers and monitoring

description: Insufficient Authentication Controls The system relies on single-factor authentication in some areas and lacks proper MFA implementation through SAML 2.0 identity provider. An attacker who obtains user credentials could access the system without being challenged for a second authentication factor.
